summary: A widely shared video falsely showed Cambodia's Senate President asking for money to fund a war with Thailand. Authorities said real footage was edited with an AI-generated fake voice track, and called it disinformation and a scam.
technical_summary: Genuine footage of a political leader was overlaid with a synthetic voice track imitating his voice, plus an AI female voice, to solicit small payments for a fictional war fund. Distribution on social platforms spread the clip before official denunciation.

summary: A Tesla rear-ended a parked fire truck on an Indiana interstate, killing the passenger and seriously injuring the driver. Federal regulators later said the car was on Autopilot and opened a broader investigation of similar crashes.
technical_summary: A Level 2 driver-assistance system that maintains speed and lane position failed to avoid a stationary emergency vehicle with lights on. Regulators identified a pattern of Autopilot crashes at first-responder scenes and are examining driver-engagement monitoring and the system's object detection.

failure_mode.quote: Tesla cars on autopilot or Traffic Aware Cruise Control encountered first-responder scenes and hit at least one emergency vehicle

severity.quote: killing an Arizona woman and seriously injuring her husband

notes: Responsibility is shared between the driver-assistance system and the driver, who remains responsible.

summary: Montana prosecutors charged a man with child sexual abuse offenses, alleging he used AI to alter images of a local child taken from her parents' public social media account. The material was found after cloud-storage tips.
technical_summary: A generative AI tool was allegedly used to manipulate photos of a real child into sexual abuse material. Detection came via automated cloud-backup reports to a child-protection center. The case applies a 2025 state law covering AI-altered abuse content.

summary: Two Houston-area women say scammers used AI-generated videos of friends to trick them into giving up account access codes. Fake sale posts and AI videos of the women were then sent to their friends, some of whom sent money.
technical_summary: Scammers used video-call and message avatars that cloned a friend's face and voice, possibly from a single image, to get access codes and take over social accounts. They then used cloned videos of the victims to sell nonexistent goods to their contacts.

summary: A Tesla reportedly left a road in Texas and struck a house at high speed, killing a woman inside. Authorities said the driver used a driver-assistance system, while Tesla later said the driver had manually overridden it. Investigations are open.
technical_summary: A Model 3 failed to stay in lane and crashed into a residence at high speed. The driver reportedly said driver-assistance was engaged, but Tesla's Autopilot lead said the driver had pressed the accelerator fully, overriding it. The cause of the loss of speed control is still under investigation.

summary: Deepfake videos and articles imitating trusted Australian doctors and celebrities were spread on Facebook and Instagram to sell unproven health supplements. One fake piece told diabetes patients to stop metformin and use a supplement instead.
technical_summary: Voice-cloned and face-synthesized videos of known doctors and celebrities, plus fake articles, were used in ads linking to supplement sites with alias branding. The campaign grew in volume and sophistication, and takedown requests to the platform reportedly failed.

summary: An AI-generated Christmas card showing the young children of a prominent royal couple spread on X as if real. Users quickly noticed sloppy editing and called it fake, and the couple's actual card had been released earlier.
technical_summary: A flawed AI-edited composite built from older public photos of two children was posted on a social platform with a forged signature. Visible artifacts, such as missing hands and feet and filter effects, led users to flag it as fake.

summary: After the Maui wildfires, Chinese influence operations spread false posts claiming the US had caused them with a secret weather weapon. Some posts used AI-generated photographs to look more credible.
technical_summary: A coordinated network of accounts posted multilingual conspiracy content with images that appeared to be AI-generated, to lend authenticity to a disinformation narrative. Researchers described it as among the first influence operations to use such tools, and impact was hard to measure.

summary: Scammers used AI to build realistic fake IRS websites and emails to trick taxpayers into giving personal and financial information. Security firms reported a sharp rise in tax-related phishing before Tax Day 2025.
technical_summary: Generative AI improved the language quality and visual fidelity of imposter websites, emails and texts impersonating a tax agency. The fakes made phishing harder to spot and drove personal data theft and financial loss.

summary: After a fatal shooting by a federal immigration agent in Minneapolis, users asked Grok to unmask the masked agent. It produced a fabricated face that spread online with a wrong name, leading to harassment of at least two uninvolved men.
technical_summary: An image-capable chatbot generated an invented unmasked face in response to user prompts. AI enhancement fills in plausible but false facial details, so the output cannot support identification. The image and an unsourced name were widely shared, causing misidentification.

summary: MIT Technology Review tested two AI job-interview tools and found they gave positive scores, including English competency ratings, to a candidate who answered in German by reading an encyclopedia entry.
technical_summary: Personality and competency scoring models used in AI interviews produced favorable scores for responses in the wrong language and unrelated content. The tests suggest the systems do not reliably evaluate what they claim to, raising validity and transparency concerns in hiring.
